profile.reading: Centeris SH2 Build-to-Suit is the second, larger building on Centeris' South Hill data center campus in Puyallup, Washington, an 86 acre site owned and operated by The Benaroya Company roughly 35 miles south of downtown Seattle. A November 2, 2017 Data Center Frontier article describes this building as a 176,000 square foot powered shell, distinct from the smaller, already operating 56,000 square foot LEED Gold SH1 building on the same campus, this registry's separate SH1 Colocation row, with an on-site substation supporting up to 50 megawatts of total campus capacity between the two buildings. This registry's own earlier research had flagged this row as a distinct, planned or future phase building given the powered shell description, consistent with that same trade press characterization. A more recent October 22, 2025 Data Center Dynamics report on the campus, referring to it as the South Hill Business and Technology Center at 1023 39th Avenue Southeast, Puyallup, Washington 98374, states current owner Centeris invested nearly 200 million dollars over the prior 18 months to expand the campus to 24 megawatts of critical load including liquid cooled racks for AI and cloud customers, though the report does not specify whether that expansion capital built out this specific SH2 shell or expanded capacity within the existing SH1 building, so this row's own build-out status as of the most recent sourcing remains uncertain rather than assumed complete. An earlier Seattle Times feature on the campus describes it as the first transpacific data hub designed to store and connect data between Asia and the US West Coast, built in 2008 and remodeled in 2011 in partnership with network provider Wave, totaling 376,000 square feet across its two buildings. The Benaroya Company is a Pacific Northwest real estate firm with more than 60 years in the region and 100 percent ownership of Centeris.

reading.body:
This facility is listed as a build-to-suit phase on Centeris's South Hill campus near Puyallup, Washington, and carries an unresolved status: the operator's own website publishes no power specifications, no street address, and no timeline for this specific building. Research flags show that the stored coordinates resolve to a Puyallup city building rather than a Centeris facility, and the actual campus location remains unconfirmed pending county parcel records.

Without published power or IT specifications, this facility cannot be sized against AI demand. The campus owner is confirmed as The Benaroya Company, a regional real estate firm, but no information about tenants, pricing, or grid connections is published.

Washington State shows 46 mapped data center facilities but only two with published power figures totaling 60 MW. This campus ranks third in the state by published capacity, yet publishes no specifications itself, making it invisible to anyone tracking actual buildout of AI-ready infrastructure. The gap between ranking and data suggests the state context may reflect earlier capacity claims that are no longer current or were never substantiated with specifications.
